the crystallization of a bacterial xylanase and the influence of polymeric substrate on the crystallization process.
the crystallization of a protein in the absence of polymeric substrate and the crystallization of complexes of the protein and substrate in the presence of substrate.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallization of xylanases from Erwinia is significantly enhanced by heating the protein to 50 degrees C prior to dispensing crystallization trials.
xylanase from E. chrysanthemi is a good model for crystallization studies, and that heat treatment of the protein is an important factor in obtaining good quality crystals.
the crystallization of E. chrysanthemi xylanase in the presence of xylan yields crystals that are suitable for X-ray diffractions studies of the enzyme-substrate complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a polymeric substrate can lead to crystallization of an enzyme in a form that is distinct from the native state.
the use of polymeric substrate in the crystallization of enzymes is not necessarily detrimental to the crystallization process.
heat treatment of protein solutions prior to setting up crystallization trials is an effective and inexpensive means of enhancing the reproducibility and quality of crystals obtained.
